task.description:
Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0423-20260905/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json's result.summary in full -- it is ISSUE-FIXER's complete diagnosis for ISS-0423/ISS-0113 and carries the fresh measurement (plain mix test: 'Finished in 1316.3 seconds (18.2s async, 1298.1s sync)', 3227 passed; mix letflow.check currently fails at N=16 on this host, unrelated ISS-0219/ISS-0222 class) and the exact line (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:206) responsible for the async-defeating global Sandbox.mode(:auto) call. Do not re-run that measurement -- build the design from it.

Also read docs/issues/ISS-0113.yaml in full: it documents a REAL ATTEMPTED FIX that was tried and reverted on 2026-08-21, with three distinct, independently-confirmed failure mechanisms when a blanket Sandbox.mode(:manual)-restore was added to provisioned_tenant!/1: (1) a test that itself later calls Sandbox.checkout/1 expecting a fresh :ok, now gets {:already, :owner}; (2) tests that spawn a second process needing genuine concurrent multi-process access to the real pool (a real FOR UPDATE lock test), which a single sandboxed connection cannot serve; (3) tests that call provision_tenant_schema!/replay_migrations! a SECOND time within the same test body, which itself needs :auto mode for Ecto.Migrator's own connection checkout to succeed. ISS-0113's own conclusion: the fix must be PER-CALLER OPT-IN (e.g. opts[:restore_sandbox], default false/unchanged), never a blanket default, because each of the 87 current TenantFixture call sites needs individual verification against these three mechanisms before being safely flipped.

Design the fix for ISS-0113 as the mechanism to unlock real async:true execution for TenantFixture call sites that do NOT hit any of the three documented failure mechanisms above. Your design artefact (in lib/letflow/design/, per this project's convention) must specify:

1. The exact opt-in mechanism on Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (signature/@spec change, default value, and what it does differently when set -- restore Sandbox.mode(:manual) + checkout after provisioning, matching the pattern already proven in user_test.exs/group_test.exs/tenant_role_test.exs/role_registry_test.exs per ISS-0113's own note that these hand-rolled helpers already do this correctly).
2. A concrete, mechanical DECISION PROCEDURE for classifying any one of the 87 current call sites as safe-to-opt-in vs not, keyed to ISS-0113's three named mechanisms (e.g.: does this test file call Sandbox.checkout/1 itself? does it spawn a second process needing concurrent DB access? does it call provision_tenant_schema!/replay_migrations! a second time?) -- this is what lets ELIXIR-DEV or a later run classify sites without re-deriving judgment per site.
3. Which specific test modules/files in THIS run's actual scope will be converted (you decide the batch size -- a partial conversion, e.g. a first tranche of files confirmed safe, is a legitimate and expected outcome; converting all 87 in one PASS is very likely too large and risky for one run. State your chosen scope and why.)
4. THE PEAK-CONCURRENT-DBCONNECTION-CHECKOUT SIZING QUESTION ISSUE-FIXER RAISED, explicitly: if N files go from serialized-by-:auto to genuinely concurrent async:true, how many of them can ExUnit actually schedule to run at once (ExUnit's own case concurrency defaults to System.schedulers_online()), and does that peak fit under the ACTIVE test run's pool_size -- both for a plain `mix test` invocation (config/test.exs's default schedulers_online()*2 pool) AND for a scripts/test_parallel.sh partition (TEST_POOL_SIZE per decision 0009/ISS-0287's formula, e.g. 5 at this host's N=16, or whatever ExUnit --max-cases effectively is at the N you choose to validate against). State the actual number your design produces as peak concurrent checkouts, and justify it is under whatever pool_size configuration you test against -- this is a HARD constraint (ISS-0224's own hazard class), not a nice-to-have. If your design's own converted batch could exceed pool_size, you must either shrink the batch, or add a mechanism (e.g. ExUnit --max-cases cap, or async concurrency limited via a group) to keep peak checkouts bounded -- state which.
5. Explicitly reconcile against decision 0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md (and its ISS-0287 addendum) -- confirm your design does not change N, does not change scripts/test_parallel.sh's own budget formula, and state the new intra-partition concern this design introduces is a genuinely NEW dimension 0009 does not cover (ISSUE-FIXER already argued this; confirm or refute it with your own reasoning).
6. Zero tests may be deleted, skipped or excluded to achieve any part of this (ISS-0423 AC4) -- your design must not touch existing test file content beyond adding the opt-in flag/restore call at identified safe call sites.

This is a design artefact only -- no implementation code. Signatures, @specs, and the decision procedure only, per this project's established design-doc convention (see any file under lib/letflow/design/ for the expected shape, e.g. lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md).
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact written to lib/letflow/design/, following this project's established shape (signatures/@specs/decision procedures, no implementation bodies)
The opt-in mechanism on provisioned_tenant!/1 is fully specified: new opts key, default value, exact behavior change
A concrete, mechanical (not judgment-based) decision procedure classifies call sites against ISS-0113's three named failure mechanisms
A specific, bounded conversion scope (which files/modules) is named for THIS run, with reasoning for why that scope and not all 87 sites at once

Peak concurrent DBConnection checkouts under the proposed scope is stated as a real number, justified against a stated pool_size (both plain mix test and a scripts/test_parallel.sh partition scenario), per decision 0009/ISS-0287
Decision 0009 and its ISS-0287 addendum are explicitly reconciled -- confirmed consistent, or an amendment proposed
No existing test file content is deleted, skipped, or has assertions weakened by this design

result.summary:
Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md. KEY CORRECTION TO THE DISPATCH'S OWN PREMISE (stated up front in the design's §0, not silently absorbed): re-counting the '87 call sites / 93 async:true files' claim directly against the current tree found that of the 46 distinct test files that actually call Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1, ZERO are declared async: true today -- every apparent async:true match was either moduledoc prose (four files quoting 'async: true' only to explain why they are async:false) or a file (mobile_tenant_config_test.exs) that mentions the function name in prose but never calls it. So fixing ISS-0113's blanket :auto leak by itself unlocks no dormant async execution; 'conversion' in this design means individually-verified async:false -> async:true flips, not un-defeating already-declared async files.

1) OPT-IN MECHANISM: new opts[:restore_sandbox] :: boolean() on provisioned_tenant!/1, default false (today's exact unchanged behavior). When true, after the existing 1-6 provisioning sequence completes unchanged, the fixture does Sandbox.mode(:manual) + a fresh Sandbox.checkout/1 (mirroring user_test.exs/group_test.exs/tenant_role_test.exs/role_registry_test.exs's own already-proven hand-rolled pattern), then registers a SECOND on_exit/1 (only when restore_sandbox: true) that restores :auto -- relying on ExUnit's LIFO on_exit ordering so the pre-existing schema-drop teardown (registered earlier, unaffected) still runs under :auto after this new callback fires. The 44 non-converted call sites' teardown path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

2) DECISION PROCEDURE, keyed to ISS-0113's three named mechanisms, applied by direct file read (not grep alone): (a) self-checkout -- does the file's test body call Sandbox.checkout/1 later, expecting :ok under ambient :auto? (b) concurrent multi-process -- does it spawn a second process (Task.start/async, spawn) doing independent real Postgres work concurrently? (c) second provisioning -- does it call provision_tenant_schema!/replay_migrations!/provisioned_tenant! a second time in the same test body? All three 'no' for EVERY test in the file (whole-file, since async: is module-wide) -> safe to flip.

3) CHOSEN SCOPE, this run: 2 files -- test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs. Both read in full: single provisioned_tenant! call site each, zero Sandbox./Task./spawn( references outside moduledoc prose, zero second provisioning calls. Verified unsafe and excluded: service_catalog_test.exs (real Task.start+Task.async holding a row lock concurrently -- mechanism b) and routers/onboarding_test.exs (doesn't call provisioned_tenant! for its own tenants at all; its own on_exit issues Sandbox.mode(:auto) directly -- flagged as OQ-1, outside this design's TenantFixture-scoped procedure). Remaining 42 files explicitly NOT classified this run (bounded first tranche, not all-46 -- rationale in design §4.3: full-file-read cost per site, prove the mechanism first, keep peak-checkout arithmetic trivially bounded, zero tolerance for a wrong classification per ISS-0423 AC4/AC6).

4) PEAK CONCURRENT DBCONNECTION CHECKOUTS: this design's own tranche adds at most 2 files' worth of async-eligible tests to the population ExUnit's scheduler-wide concurrency (System.schedulers_online(), no --max-cases override anywhere in the repo -- confirmed by grep) already governs. Plain mix test: pool_size = schedulers_online()*2 = 32 on the 16-core verification host; ExUnit's own scheduling ceiling is already 16 concurrent async cases system-wide (147 pre-existing async:true files -> 149 after this change, but the ceiling stays pinned to schedulers_online(), not file count) -- 16 against pool_size 32, 16 connections of slack, unconditionally, before and after this design's addition. scripts/test_parallel.sh partition (N=16, TEST_POOL_SIZE=5 per decision 0009's own verified arithmetic): each partition's own async-eligible file count is a small fraction of 149 spread across 16 partitions (~9/partition average), well under both the 16-wide scheduler ceiling and that partition's pool_size=5; where a partition's own pool is the binding constraint, DBConnection queues (backpressure) rather than crashing, exactly the intra-partition degradation decision 0009's own text already accepts. This design's 2-file addition is a ~1.4% (2/147) proportional increase to a dynamic that already exists today, not a new peak-checkout regime -- stated as the real number (2 files / bounded by the pre-existing 16-wide ceiling) rather than left unquantified.

5) DECISION 0009/ISS-0287 RECONCILIATION: confirmed consistent, not amended. This design touches none of TEST_MAX_CONNECTIONS/TEST_CONNECTION_HEADROOM/TEST_MIN_POOL_SIZE/TEST_SUPERUSER_RESERVED/TEST_NONPOOL_CONNECTION_RESERVE/TEST_POOL_SIZE, and does not change N-derivation. Confirmed (not refuted) ISSUE-FIXER's own framing: 0009 governs the CROSS-partition question (does N x TEST_POOL_SIZE fit under max_connections); this design's own concern is a genuinely distinct INTRA-partition question (how many of one partition's own TEST_POOL_SIZE connections its own async tests might hold at once) that 0009 treats as a black box by design, not a gap in 0009 -- resolved for this tranche's small size by direct arithmetic (§5.3), with the threshold at which a future larger tranche would need a new mechanism (--max-cases cap, or a custom concurrency-limited grouping) stated explicitly in §5.4 rather than left for a future run to rediscover from scratch.

6) NO TEST CONTENT DELETED/SKIPPED/WEAKENED: only opts[:restore_sandbox] added to tenant_fixture.ex (new optional key, old default preserved) and async: false -> async: true + restore_sandbox: true added at secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs's existing provisioned_tenant! call sites. Zero assertion text touched anywhere.
issues: OQ-1 (design §7): test/letflow/routers/onboarding_test.exs manages its own ad-hoc Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call inside cleanup_onboarded_tenant!/1, independent of TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 -- this design's decision procedure is TenantFixture-call-site-scoped and does not cover hand-rolled :auto users; needs a separate design pass or a deliberate scope decision before that file (or others like it) could be considered for async conversion.

OQ-2/OQ-3 (design §7): 42 of the 46 TenantFixture-calling files remain unclassified by this run (deliberate, bounded first tranche); this design's classifications for the 2 converted files are by-inspection only, not yet confirmed by a real mix test/scripts/test_parallel.sh run -- that verification belongs to TEST-RUNNER/ELIXIR-DEV per this pipeline's normal division of labor.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate this design (opt-in mechanism completeness, decision-procedure mechanicalness, scope justification, peak-checkout arithmetic, decision-0009 reconciliation, zero-assertion-change compliance) before ELIXIR-DEV implements the 3 file changes listed in design §8.
